sentence: 113	Pt, ******, is a 10 1/2 year old male who is diagnosed with cardiomyopathy and pulmonary hypertension of unknown origin who is being referred for heart transplant Psychosocial Assessment.
Information for this assessment was obtained through an interview with the pt's mother and review of the medical records.
SW spent 60 minutes of face to face time with patient and family.
Living situation:  **, ******, lives with his mother and sister in ** *****, VI.
They have been staying with an aunt (********* ******) who resides in Jacksonville while in the US.
This is a single family, 3 bedroom, 2 bath home.
It has city water and central heating and a/c.

Demographics:  Mother: ****** ****  DOB:  **/**/****           Age: 34  Employment:  ****** Islands ****** Department  Phone:  ***-***-**** (cell)     Father: deceased (2010)     Siblings:  Sister: ******* ******, twin, no medical problems     Support systems:  Most of the family resides in the ****** Islands.
However, mom has an aunt who resides in Jacksonville who is a support for the family.
Aunt ********* has a car and is able to assist with transportation.
She also has opened her home to the family.
Mom also has a sister who resides in the ****** Islands, and will be keeping ******* when she returns home in a few weeks to go to school.
In addition, ****** has a fiancé who resides in ** ******.
He will be coming to West **** ***** for back surgery on **** **.

She is hopeful that he will be able to come here for a while after he *********** from the surgery, prior to returning to St ******.     ****** does not have a car in the US, and is not comfortable driving here.

She states she is used to driving on the left side of the road, and she is used to rural ***** with very little traffic.  ****** states she does have a separate insurance policy that covers ambulance transport, should ****** be allowed to wait for a heart at the aunt's home.
The family identifies as *********.  ****** states that she had not been attending church due to her work schedule.
However, the children had been attending ********* **** her mother, prior to her death 4 months ago.
She states ******'s faith is a source of strength for him.
Due to his autism spectrum disorder, he does not have a lot of friends or supports outside of the family.
He is reportedly close to his twin sister, '*****'.
Both ****** and ***** are entering the 6th grade.  ****** was enrolled in an *** curriculum.
She is hopeful that the school can send this curriculum here for him to continue progressing.
She is open to hospital homebound for him, but states he would benefit from *** or autism-based curriculum.
Course of illness:     ****** is a 10 ½ yr old male with cardiomyopathy of unknown origin.
He became symptomatic about a year ago.
He was diagnosed with obstructive sleep apnea and then asthma.

After no improvement, he was referred to cardiologist two weeks ago, and found to have severe mitral regurgitation, ** ******************, moderately reduced LV systolic dysfunction, diastolic dysfunction, and pulmonary hypertension.
A cardiac catheterization was obtained revealing severely elevated LVEDP with resulting elevated PA pressures in the setting of a normal transpulmonary gradient.
He was started on Milrinone following the catheterization.
He was then transferred to us for heart transplant evaluation.
Financial Situation:     ****** is covered by ***** insurance through his mother's employer.
He is also covered by ******* through his father's estate.
In addition, he has a policy with *****, and a policy for ambulance transport.
Both ****** and his sister receive a death benefit through social security from their father's estate.  ****** was also financially supporting the family with her employment income.
She is in the process of completing paperwork that allows ********* to donate PTO to her.
She believes she will have enough donated PTO to financially support her through ********.       ***** has a transplant housing benefit of $10,000.
This will cover 5-6 months of housing at the ******.
Mom states she hopes to keep the donated PTO  or do whatever is necessary to stay employed at ** PD so she can maintain the ***** insurance.
Eventually, however, she states she plans to permanently relocate to ******* so that ****** will be closer for his medical care.
She will seek local employment at that time.
Fundraising was also discussed.
Information on Childrens ***** Transplant Association was provided.
Family History:     There is history of multiple medical problems in the family on both sides.
******'s father passed away from a heart attack in 2010.
He had a history of heart problems prior to this. *******, ****** is unsure what his diagnosis was.
******'s mother passed away 4 months ago from ***, diabetes, and hypertension.
She also had a history of breast cancer.
In addition, ******'s brother passed away at age 22 from a pulmonary embolism.
Her grandmother also passed away from a pulmonary embolism.     ****** has diabetes and is on insulin and medications for this.
She has enough for about a month, but then will need to follow up with an endocrine physician.
She also states she needs to see gyn by ********.
She is covered by ***** insurance.
SW will assist her in finding local providers who accept this insurance.
SW also advised her **** *** ******** accepts ***** if she needs to get refills on any meds while here.     ****** has been diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, and a mood disorder.
He is allergic to *********, and has been on abilify for the last 3 years.
He has been on multiple other psychotropic meds in the past several years.
He was started on Prozac and clonidine in *** or **** of this year.
These were managed by his PCP, as the psychiatrist moved to one of the other islands.
He has not seen psychiatry since 2015.  ****** states he likely needs to go up on some of the dosages since they were started in *** with the idea of titrating up.
However, as he became ill and they came here, this has not been done.
She states she is unsure about doing too many changes with them currently however, since his cardiac meds are being adjusted too.
She is open to psych consult in regards to this.       ****** denies any other history of mental health issues in the family.
The family denies any family  history of substance abuse.
She denies any legal involvement, and states she would be unable to be employed at the police department if she had any criminal history.
Adherence:  There are no concerns for adherence that have been identified.  ****** states ****** does well with taking pills, but does not like to take liquid meds.
She states he is cooperative with taking them, and she feels comfortable administering them to him.  ****** appears to be an attentive mom who is able to provide structure for him.
She states she is particularly big on him having a structured bedtime.
The entire family unit is overweight.
It will be important for ****** to maintain a heart healthy diet after transplant to protect his new heart and keep it as healthy as possible.
It has been demonstrated to improve patient success when the whole family ******** a healthy diet and exercise routine after transplant.
It is unclear if ****** is receptive to making changes in this area.
Assessment and recommendations:     ****** just became aware of the possibility of ****** needing a heart transplant recently.
She is still processing this information.
She states it is easier for her to cope with tangible things at first, such as getting PTO donated etc.
She states, however, that she will do whatever it takes to give him the best chance of survival.
She states she has lost too many family members recently and she cannot lose him too.
She is in agreement with moving forward with transplant.       ****** does not really know about the possibility of transplant.
He becomes anxious rather easily and Is limited in his understanding of things.
Mom gave an example that he became very anxious when taken for MRI.
He heard another pt crying and assumed he would be hurt during the procedure.
Mom then showed him a video of what a MRI machine is, and described it as going into a ****** ship that is really noisy.
She explained they would give him something to sleep during it because of the noise.
He was then able to calm down and complete the procedure.
She has told him that his heart is sick and that he is here to work on getting it fixed.
He has never had surgery other than tonsillectomy previously.
SW discussed involving Child **** to assist him in coping with heart transplant issues.  ****** is open to this, but wants to wait to give details about heart transplant later down the road.

IMPRESSION:     (Low Risk - 1; Moderate Risk - 2; High Risk - 3; Severe Risk - 4)     Home Environment/Transportation -  2     Family Background & Social Support -  1     Financial/Insurance  - 2     Mental Health/Substance Abuse - 2     Involvement with *** Enforcement/Child Protection -  1     Adherence - 1     Understanding of medical situation & transplant process -  2     Health Literacy -  1     Coping Skills - 1     Total:  13 Low/Moderate Risk     The family scores as low/moderate risk in regards to psychosocial contra-indicators to transplant.
The primary concern is the stress related to being so far from home and adapting to being in a different country with more limited support immediately available.
Mom will be trying to support ****** here while her daughter is in ** *****.
She is also likely going to experience some financial burdens depending on how much PTO is donated to her.

Housing and transportation locally is another challenge, although insurance will provide almost 6 months of housing post-transplant, and the aunt may be able to assist with transportation when possible.
Recommendations are listed below:     Recommendations:  *Provide ongoing education to the family about heart transplant and post-transplant care.
Use teach-back method to ensure that the patient and family understands what is being explained.

*Provide fundraising and financial resources to assist the family with displacement expenses that arise secondary to transplant    *Assist with ****** getting the counseling and psychotropic meds he needs to stay as emotionally stable as possible  *Engage Child **** in assisting ****** with coping with the medical procedures and surgery etc  *Connect mom with resources to address her own medical needs           ****** ******** LCSW  Pediatric Heart/ Lung Transplant Team  ***-***-****
